episodes.title: Anti-Man BDSM Cult That Made Video Games & Invented Cosplay (Nothing Changes)
episodes.description:
A deep dive into the strange history of a 1970s fantasy religion that broke containment into real-world communes, immersive boarding school experiences, and early computer game development. The episode traces its evolution from Oxford-area writings and goddess-focused observances through anti-modern settlements in Ireland, the creation of text adventures on Commodore 64 and ZX Spectrum hardware, and later publishing efforts.

Listeners explore how the group attempted financial self-sustainability, the role of role-play and discipline practices in its later phases, connections to far-right materials, and why the movement ultimately remained a niche online remnant rather than a lasting community. The discussion highlights themes of invented religions, alternate reality games before the term existed, and the challenges of building sustainable new belief systems.

episodes.title: Buddhist Cult At The Nexus of The Tech Elite (It Wants to Kill Your Soul)
episodes.description:
A deep investigation into Maple, a high-control organization with roots in effective altruism and Buddhist philosophy. The discussion covers its leader's past statements on human extinction, ties to major tech funders, isolation practices, financial extraction from members, and plans for an AI system to enforce total control over society.

Hosts contrast these goals with their own focus on human flourishing and technological progress. The episode examines whistleblower accounts, funding sources like the Survival and Flourishing Fund, and why such groups represent a unique risk within elite intellectual circles.

episodes.title: How A Gay Jew Rewrote Core Catholic Doctrine in the 1960s (This is CRAZY)
episodes.description:
Is Vatican II the result of a "gay Jew infiltrating the Catholic Church"? Malcolm and Simone Collins dive deep into the shocking story of Gregory Baum — a matrilineal Jew, former Catholic priest, and openly gay man who authored the first draft of Nostra Aetate, one of the most controversial documents of the Second Vatican Council.

In this episode, they explore:
• Baum’s background, conversion, active homosexuality while writing key Church documents, and later life
• The content and lasting impact of Nostra Aetate on Catholic teaching regarding Jews, other religions, and interfaith dialogue
• Why many traditional Catholics view Vatican II with deep suspicion
• The broader implications for Church authority, doctrine, and demographics

A wild, uncomfortable, and thought-provoking discussion on faith, identity, institutional capture, and theology. What do you think — infiltration, urban monoculture influence, or something else?

Watch until the end for Malcolm & Simone's unfiltered reactions.
